# Supply Chain & Provenance Tracking

This dimension covers how AI-generated code affects software supply chain security.

## Package Hallucination ("Slopsquatting")

AI models systematically recommend non-existent packages, creating a novel supply chain attack vector.

### Hallucination Rates

| Source | Models | Rate |
|--------|--------|------|
| [6] (USENIX) | Commercial models (aggregate) | 5.2% |
| [6] (USENIX) | Open-source models (aggregate) | 21.7% |
| [21] (Snyk) | GPT-3.5-Turbo | ~20% |
| [21] (Snyk) | GPT-4 | ~20% |
| [21] (Snyk) | Gemini Pro (Bard) | 64.5% |
| [20] (OpenSSF) | Aggregate | 19.7% |

The USENIX study [6] analyzed 576,000 code samples across 16 LLMs and found 205,474 unique hallucinated package names. Open-source models show approximately 4x higher hallucination rates than commercial alternatives [6].

### Attack Methodology

Four-stage slopsquatting attack [21]:
1. AI generates non-existent package name
2. Developer integrates fictional dependency
3. Attacker registers hallucinated name with malicious payload
4. Installation triggers backdoor

**Real-world proof:** An empty package named "huggingface-cli" received 30,000+ downloads in 3 months [21].

### Mitigations
- Curated package whitelists / lockfiles with hash verification [20]
- Real-time SCA vulnerability detection [21]
- CI/CD pipeline dependency verification before installation [20]
- Generate SBOM using SPDX or CycloneDX [20]
- Track provenance via in-toto attestations [20]
- Pin container images by SHA256 digest [20]

## Prompt Injection Attacks on Coding Assistants

AI coding assistants themselves are attack vectors for supply chain compromise.

### GitHub Copilot Agent Attack [15]
- **Vector:** Hidden prompt injection in GitHub Issues using HTML `<picture>` tags
- **Mechanism:** When maintainers assign Copilot to implement fixes, injected instructions compromise generated PRs
- **Payload:** Modifies `uv.lock` with malicious wheel URL for flask-babel; enables bash execution via HTTP headers
- **No CVEs assigned**

### Argument Injection in AI Agents [16]
- **CVE-2025-54795:** Claude Code inverse prompt injection
- **GHSA-534m-3w6r-8pqr:** Cursor agentic IDE command injection
- **Amazon Q:** Command injection (August 2025)
- **Root cause:** Agents permit "safe" utilities (find, grep, git) without validating command-line flags
- **Key finding:** "Safe command allowlists are fundamentally flawed" — command flag variety makes comprehensive filtering "unsupportable" [16]

### Mitigations [16]
- Always use `--` argument separator before user input
- `subprocess.run(shell=False)`
- Container-based sandboxing as primary control

## AI Bill of Materials (AI-BOM)

Traditional SBOMs are insufficient for AI systems where behavior is determined by data as much as code [31].

### What AI-BOM Tracks Beyond SBOM [31]
- Models and versions with lineage and parameter changes
- Training and fine-tuning datasets (sources, licensing)
- Data origins with approval status and sensitivity
- Evaluation artifacts documenting known limitations
- Inference services and third-party AI dependencies
- Deployment details: endpoints, access controls, monitoring

Key principle: "Each element is tied to ownership. Someone approved the data. Someone selected the base model" [31].

### Risk Vectors SBOM Misses [31]
- Poisoned or improperly licensed training data
- Hidden behaviors in pretrained models
- Silent weight updates from third-party providers
- Malicious instructions in documents that models parse

### Standards
- SPDX and CycloneDX for SBOM generation [20]
- In-toto attestations for provenance [20]
- SLSA framework for supply chain integrity [29]
- ISO/IEC 42001 and EU AI Act reference AI-BOM concepts [31]

## SLSA Framework

SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) provides a vendor-neutral framework with four escalating compliance tiers for preventing tampering, improving integrity, and securing packages [29]. Provenance generation — documented evidence of artifact origin, build process, and transformations — is the initial implementation step [29].

## Gaps and Limitations

- No study quantifies SCA effectiveness at detecting hallucinated packages before installation
- AI-BOM standardization is nascent; no universal format exists
- SLSA has not been formally extended for AI-generated code artifacts specifically
- No data on what percentage of developers verify AI-suggested packages before installation
- OpenSSF Model Signing specification details were not retrieved in this session
